lines: Peace to you. The barley is late and my knees are early. If you hear anything worth the walk, come and tell an old man.

annotate.text: Ezra says the words remind him of the prophet Isaiah.
Ezra says what Hannah describes puts him in mind of Isaiah's 'voice in the wilderness'.

lines: You have been listening to the road talk, I see. Sit a moment.
A man crying in the wilderness, baptizing in the Jordan, saying the kingdom of heaven is at hand. I have turned it over since morning.

The prophet Isaiah wrote: 'The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.' I do not say this John is anything. I say the words came to mind, and they have not left.
If I knew that, I would be a rich teacher in Jerusalem and not an old man with bad knees.
Go and see, if your heart tells you to. Go with open eyes, and come back and tell me what you saw.
Have you been to the river? No? Then why are you standing in front of an old man's door? Go and see. Come back and tell me.
